chunks: It has been narrated: 'When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) completed his rituals, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to depart, so he left. The mother of Isma'il passed away, and he buried her in the Hijr and enclosed it with stones so that her grave would not be stepped on. Isma'il (peace be upon him) remained alone. When the following year came, Allah gave permission to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) for the pilgrimage and the building of the Kaaba. The Arabs used to perform pilgrimage to the House, but it was in ruins, although its foundations were known. When the people departed, Isma'il (peace be upon him) gathered stones and placed them in the interior of the Kaaba.'

When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) arrived, he and Isma'il uncovered it, and it was a single red stone. Allah revealed to him: 'Place its construction upon it.' He sent down four angels to him. When the construction was complete, he sat on each corner and called out: 'Come to the Hajj, come to the Hajj!' If he had called 'Come, O people, to the Hajj,' only those living at that time would have performed it. But he called 'Come to the Hajj,' and the people responded while still in the loins of their fathers and the wombs of their mothers: 'Here I am, O Caller of Allah, here I am, O Caller of Allah.'

So whoever responded once will perform Hajj once, and whoever responded ten times will perform ten Hajj pilgrimages, and whoever did not respond will not perform Hajj. Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them) were placing stones and raising the foundations, while the angels handed them materials, until the height reached twelve cubits.

When they reached the location of the Stone, Abu Qubays called out to him: 'O Ibrahim, I have a trust for you.' So it gave him the Stone, and he placed it in its position. He prepared two doors for it, one to enter from and one to exit from, and they placed a threshold and a covering of palm leaves on its doors.

The Kaaba was uncovered. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) departed after completing the House, and Isma'il (peace be upon him) remained. Isma'il married a woman from the Amalekites, but he separated from her, and then married another woman from the Himyar tribe, who was wise.

She looked at the two doors of the House and said to Isma'il (peace be upon him): 'Why do you not hang two curtains over these two doors, one here and one there?' He said to her: 'Yes.' So she made two curtains for the House, each twelve cubits long, and Isma'il (peace be upon him) hung them over the two doors.

That pleased her, so she said: 'Why do I not sew clothing for the Kaaba to cover it entirely, for these stones are unsightly?' Isma'il (peace be upon him) said to her: 'Certainly.' So she hastened to do that and sent to her people to ask them to spin thread. And indeed, the spinning of women for one another originated from this.

Whenever she finished a piece, she hung it. When the Hajj season arrived, one side of the Kaaba remained uncovered. She said to Isma'il (peace be upon him): 'What shall we do with this side?' So they covered it with palm-leaf mats.

When the season came, the Arabs saw this and were impressed. They said: 'We should offer gifts to the caretaker of this House.' From then on, the custom of offering gifts (al-hady) began. Each tribe of the Arabs would bring something to the Kaaba, whether silver or other items, until a large amount was gathered.

They removed those palm-leaf mats and completed the covering, and hung two doors on the House. The Kaaba was not roofed, so Isma'il placed columns in it like the wooden columns you see today, and roofed it with palm stalks, smoothing it with clay.

The Arabs from the surrounding areas came, entered the Kaaba, and saw its structure. They said: 'The caretaker of this House should receive more.' When the following year came, the gifts arrived, but Isma'il (peace be upon him) did not know what to do with them. Allah revealed to him: 'Slaughter them and feed them to the pilgrims.'

The water of Zamzam dried up, and Isma'il complained to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the lack of water. Allah revealed to Ibrahim and commanded him to dig. He, Isma'il, and Jibril (peace be upon him) dug until the water appeared. He struck the four corners of the well, saying 'In the name of Allah' with each strike, and it gushed forth with four springs.

Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Drink, O Ibrahim, and pray for your descendants to be blessed with it. Pour it upon yourself and circumambulate this House. This is the water that Allah, the Exalted, provided for Isma'il and his offspring.'
As for the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'In it are clear signs, the station of Ibrahim.'

One of these signs is that when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) stood on the stone, his footprints were imprinted on it. The second is the Stone, and the third is the dwelling of Isma'il (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الْحِجْر: The semi-circular wall enclosing part of the Kaaba
key_terms.الْخَصَف: Mats made of woven palm leaves
key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Kaaba, the cube-shaped building in Mecca
key_terms.الْهَدْي: Offerings or gifts brought to the Kaaba
key_terms.زَمْزَم: The sacred spring of water in Mecca
key_terms.مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The Station of Ibrahim, a specific site within the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What is the historical account of the construction of the Kaaba and the origin of Zamzam according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* elaborates on the primordial construction of the Kaaba, highlighting the collaborative role of Ibrahim, Isma'il, and the Angel Jibril in establishing the sanctuary and the Zamzam spring. It provides a detailed exegetical basis for the 'clear signs' (*Ayat Bayyinat*) mentioned in the Quran, identifying the footprint of Ibrahim, the Foundation Stone, and the dwelling of Isma'il as these divine markers, while also tracing the ritualistic origins of Hajj and offerings to these early events.
